subject: verify insurance before relying on the screen
preheader: availability, coverage, deductibles, and price are property-specific.
headline: Insurance needs a current property-specific quote.
body: Insurance availability, covered perils, exclusions, deductibles, replacement-cost assumptions, and premiums vary by property, carrier, borrower, and effective date. A national or state percentage is not a substitute for a quote.
For illustration, changing an entered annual premium from $1,800 to $2,800 reduces modeled NOI by $1,000. That arithmetic is a sensitivity example, not a forecast of premium growth or property value.

Hazard exposure and carrier eligibility can also affect whether a quoted policy provides the coverage a lender or owner expects. Review wind, flood, wildfire, liability, loss-of-rents, and other applicable terms with qualified professionals.
Obtain current written quotes for the actual ownership and occupancy plan. If future costs are uncertain, model more than one documented scenario instead of applying a universal annual growth rate.

TrueCap does not auto-adjust insurance by state or hazard zone. Enter a current property-specific quote, keep the assumption editable, and model a higher expense case when local wind, flood, wildfire, or carrier conditions warrant it.
